Diabetes mellitus may have a minimal impact on the diagnostic accuracy of Fluorodeoxyglucose-Positron Emission Tomography (FDG-PET) for cervical cancer. In comparison with its accuracy in non-DM patients, FDG-PET has shown that the efficacy of PET in diagnosing cervical cancer is not significantly reduced in patients with diabetes mellitus.

However, it's essential to note that this does not mean that diabetes completely affects the diagnostic process. Rather, diabetic patients may require more extensive and frequent imaging studies due to potential complications related to their condition.

The current consensus is that FDG-PET can be used as a diagnostic tool for cervical cancer, but its accuracy may vary depending on individual factors, such as the presence of diabetes mellitus. To optimize diagnosis and treatment, it's crucial to consider patients' overall health status, including any underlying conditions like diabetes, when interpreting PET scan results.

Overall, while diabetes mellitus might have some impact on FDG-PET accuracy, its influence is likely to be minimal in most cases.
